headline: High: shared MCP/API surfaces and broad egress create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action risks; OpenMetadata↔RD-Agent is not directly documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: OpenMetadata exposes MCP/server-style surfaces and webhooks, while RD-Agent runs browsers and consumes external APIs. That creates a plausible bridge where content from one can be treated as instructions by the other, even though no direct pairwise interaction is documented. Uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF OpenMetadata content is forwarded into RD-Agent prompts or browser-visible pages without sanitization, injection is possible.
IF either agent parses the other's output as instructions via MCP, webhooks, or copied text, the attack path exists.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of untrusted OpenMetadata text into RD-Agent prompts.
Add a provenance tag to all cross-agent messages.
Require allowlisted schemas for MCP/webhook payloads.
Review any browser-scraped content before it reaches agent prompts.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction-stripping middleware.

B_data_leakage.rationale: OpenMetadata touches governance, lineage, and memory/tribal-knowledge data, while RD-Agent handles logs, execution traces, and secrets plus broad API egress. If they share a workspace or exchange files, sensitive metadata can leak from A into B and then out through B's networked APIs. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace, so this remains medium.
conditions: IF OpenMetadata exports governance or lineage artifacts into a shared directory, RD-Agent can read them.
IF RD-Agent sends those artifacts to OpenAI/Azure/DeepSeek/Kaggle APIs, leakage occurs.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Block RD-Agent from reading OpenMetadata export directories.
Redact secrets and governance fields before handoff.
Restrict RD-Agent egress to approved endpoints only.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation and DLP scanning.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents support multiple instances, and OpenMetadata can act through APIs/SDKs/events/webhooks while RD-Agent uses APIs and files/logs. Overlapping writes to shared mutable resources are plausible, but the profiles do not show unrestricted writes to the same directory or shared locks, so the conflict is real but not proven high.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same workspace, log directory, or API-backed resource without locking, conflicts can occur.
IF either agent mutates shared metadata or experiment state concurrently, last-write-wins corruption is possible.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Serialize writes with a lock file or queue.
Make one agent read-only on shared resources.
Snapshot shared state before concurrent runs.
requires-engineering: add optimistic-concurrency checks to shared stores.

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenMetadata produces governance and lineage context that RD-Agent could treat as authoritative when generating research or automation outputs. RD-Agent also has broad API access, so a mistaken upstream fact can cascade into downstream actions or reports. Because no direct orchestration is documented, this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF RD-Agent consumes OpenMetadata outputs without verification, upstream errors can propagate.
IF RD-Agent uses those outputs to generate reports, code, or API calls, the error cascades downstream.
mitigations: Insert a human review step between agents.
Require RD-Agent to cite source records before acting.
Compare OpenMetadata outputs against a second source.
Limit RD-Agent to draft-only mode for cross-agent inputs.
requires-engineering: add verification gates and provenance checks.

E_compliance.rationale: OpenMetadata touches governance and memory/tribal knowledge, while RD-Agent handles financial reports, competition datasets, logs, and secrets and can egress broadly to third-party APIs. That combination can create retention or residency mismatches if regulated data is routed through RD-Agent. The profiles do not specify a concrete jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the safest supported level.
conditions: IF regulated data from OpenMetadata is forwarded into RD-Agent's API calls, compliance obligations may be triggered.
IF retention policies differ between OpenMetadata exports and RD-Agent logs, policy mismatch occurs.
mitigations: Classify data before handoff.
Exclude regulated records from RD-Agent inputs.
Shorten log retention on both sides.
Document the data-processing boundary.
requires-engineering: add residency and retention policy enforcement.
